title: Context strip
summary: Adds P16 Context strip (draft): when an engine's controls pick part of a bigger fixed whole (a multisample synth's zones, a long wavetable, a built-in recording) and the drawing is a close-up, a small static locator of the whole sits under the header; plus the narrow craft.md exception.
rationale: Asked for by the guidelines' owner on 2026-11-04: engines can carry a top strip with grid context, such as where on a keyboard a multisample engine is, or where on a sample or waveform. Grounded in open-xy staging 6b2d113: the display Input has note activity but no pitch, a sampler-based engine plays one sample chromatically from a root key, and the sample overview is 96 bins whose begin/end markers follow every edit including stockShift trims. No screen has used it yet, so it's marked a draft pattern.

changes.content:
## P16 · Context strip

**The idea.** A draft pattern: no audited screen uses it yet; the mock in its proposal (`training/proposals/2026-11-04-context-strip/mock-rest.png`, a multisample synth) shows the intent. Some engines play from something bigger than one picture: a multisample synth's zones across the keyboard, a long wavetable, a recording built into the engine. When the controls pick part of that whole and the drawing is a close-up of the part, I put a small, static map of the whole under the header: a ruler of the whole and an open bracket on the part the controls pick. Each half of the bracket uses the close-up's corner form, the same 7 px arms joined by a short upright, so the bracket and the frame read as the same mark; that's what ties the two together. The bracket is shorter, heavier and brighter, because it's the part that moves; the drawing stays the picture every control changes, and the map only answers "which part of the whole is this?". It's the top-edge partner to P5's activity strip: that one says what's happening, this one says where you are.

**Why it works.** A close-up loses its frame of reference. With one zone's sample drawn large, the player can't tell which part of the keyboard it covers; with one frame of a long table drawn large, they can't tell how far through it they are. A locator is how drawings have always answered that, so it reads as part of the drawing rather than an interface: no slider, no filled bar echoing the header, no text.

**When it's there.** Only when both hold: the controls select part of a whole that the drawing doesn't show, and I can say in one sentence what the map tells the player that the drawing doesn't. Then it's part of the resting page, as `craft.md` allows. Otherwise there's no context strip, not even while a control turns.

- **Not P4.** When the whole is a short ordered set the drawing can stack (P4's five or six layers), the stack already shows where you are. P16 is for wholes a stack can't show: a span of the keyboard, a table too long to layer.
- **Not P13.** If a control's only picture is a keyboard (a scale, a kit's spacing), that's P13's corner keyboard.
- **Not a sampler.** A sample engine's obvious subject is its sample overview (`categories.md`), so a map of the sample would usually draw the same material twice. A synth that carries its own recording is different: it gets no overview, so its drawing can be a close-up and the map shows where it sits.

**Build it.**

- **Drawn in the screen's language.** The ruler, bracket and corner marks belong to the drawing's own language (`craft.md`, One drawing language): an atlas gets a locator inset, a section drawing gets a detail mark.
- **Where and how big.** About 6 px under the header (below y 20 with the stock header, below y 38 with the two-page header, `tokens.json` → `header`) and about 10 px tall: my starting values, slimmer than P5's 16 px bottom strip (`body.stripTop`–`stripBottom`). It spans exactly the close-up's frame (the frame's corner marks sit at the map's two ends), not the header's columns, and the gap lets the drawing own it; together those keep it from reading as a second header row.
- **The ruler is static artwork and a guide.** The whole is the engine's own fixed data (its zone map, its table, its recording), so the ruler is authored once and never redraws. Its marks are uniform and sparse, on whole pixels, hairline (1 px) in `#646464`: a keyboard gets a tick per C, a table a tick every nth frame so ticks stay at least 3 px apart, with n chosen for the table's length. A strip w px wide gives w/keys px a key and 12 × that between C ticks (480 px over all 128 notes is 3.75 and 45; the mock's 384 px over six octaves is 5.33 and 64). Zones are told apart by position: the baseline is 2 px in `#646464`, broken by a 3 px gap at each split, not by shade.
- **The bracket is two nodes.** A left and a right piece in `#AFAFAF`, 1.5 px, about 6 px tall, each one closed outline (8 points): two corners with 7 px horizontal arms joined by an upright. It sits above the baseline, at least 1 px clear of it, with each upright centred over its split gap, so the splits it points at stay open; the same offset on both sides. It's open in the middle, so its width follows the selection by moving the pieces, never by scaling. Driven by the controls through `Input` like every other part, easing 0.15–0.2 s. Turning it costs two nodes; at rest it costs nothing. The brightest thing on screen stays in the drawing.
- **The close-up's frame.** Four corner marks at the map's ends and the drawing's top and bottom, each one closed outline with 7 px legs both ways, hairline (1 px) in `#646464`. The same corner form and arm as the bracket; taller, lighter and quieter on purpose.

**Pitfalls.**

- **Possible isn't the bar.** open-xy says what the device can draw; the OP-XY's own look decides what belongs on the page. A map that's buildable but busy, bright, filled or labelled fails here even if it lints clean.
- **It doesn't answer notes.** The display input has note activity but no pitch (`draw.hpp`, `Input`), so a keyboard map can't show the key under the player's finger, and it doesn't flare either: a note is answered by the drawing (`craft.md`, Motion). The map is still.
- **Context, not a control's channel.** The bracket sliding along the ruler clears the 24 px position floor but changes too little of the screen to pass a control's perceptibility alone; the control still has to move the drawing.
- **No leader lines.** A straight line from the moving bracket to a fixed corner would have to turn and change length as the bracket moves: turning is a tilt, which this repo doesn't do to parts, and a uniform scale would thicken it. The only other way is to reshape it on every turn, which spends a mutable outline. The matching marks do the job for free.
- **Don't repeat the header.** The header shows the value in real units; the map shows where it sits.
- **One strip at rest.** Header, map, drawing and P5's bottom strip make four bands, which is a panel. With a context map, a bottom strip only shows while its own control is in use.
- **Leaving draft.** The server never draws a discipline into a design pass, so I try it on purpose, as the focus of a frames pass. It stops being a draft when an audited library screen uses it and its card says what the map added.

It's drawn as a static locator in the drawing's own language, never as a bar, a slider or a row of cells. Anywhere else there's no context strip.

Also: the owner asked that patterns stay true to the OP-XY's look, not just what open-xy allows, so 'Possible isn't the bar' is a pitfall and the strip is held to stock greys, no icons, no text.
